summary: Redwood AE and SE walked NovaPay through the Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs features. Focus was on root-cause debugging for latency spikes and failed responses, filtering by request-id, and how to use prefix/KV cache diagnostics. Customer interested in pilot on Dedicated vs Hosted, SOC2 and VPC controls. Agreed next steps to run a 2-hour benchmark and share security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-11-13 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Aisha Khan, Marco Silva (Redwood); Jared Liu, Maya Patel, Samir Desai (NovaPay)

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Aisha from Redwood, and Marco our SE is with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jared: Hey Aisha, doing well, thanks. Ready to see what you've got.
[00:08] Maya: Yeah thanks, we got about 40 minutes. We wanted a console walkthrough focusing on tracing and request logs because we're seeing intermittent latency spikes in prod.
[00:15] Marco: Great, that's exactly what we'll cover — tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Quick agenda: show tracing UI, how to pivot to request logs, use case for failed responses, and then some recommendations for configs — autoscale, KV cache, and quantization notes.
[00:28] Samir: Also we'll ask some security questions — VPC, KMS, audit logs.
[00:31] Marco: Yep we'll address those.

[01:05] Marco: (screen share) OK, starting with the trace timeline. You'll see aggregated latency by route, colored bands for token generation vs model compute vs network. Here we can zoom into a 5-minute window.
[01:20] Maya: Quick question — does the trace ingest every token or is it sampled?
[01:24] Marco: Good question. By default we sample at 10% for high-volume routes to keep storage reasonable, but you can set per-route sampling or turn on full capture for a window during a benchmark.
[01:36] Jared: So for our payments flow we'd want full capture for the pilot window.
[01:39] Marco: Exactly — you can toggle full capture for 1–4 hours.

[02:05] Marco: Here is a spike example, notice the heavy tail during model compute. If we hover, we show model variant, host id, and kernel selection.
[02:17] Aisha: Also note the fallback — you can see when requests hit smaller quantized variant as an Econ fallback.
[02:24] Maya: Sometimes we see lower quality after fallback; can we control fallback thresholds?
[02:28] Marco: Yes, in rollout policies you can set latency vs cost thresholds — immediate fallback, or a gradual A/B with auto rollback.

[03:10] Marco: Now pivot to a single request trace. Each trace ties to a request-id you can copy into request logs.
[03:16] Samir: Are request-ids persisted to our logs — can we correlate with our app logs?
[03:20] Marco: We emit request-id in response headers and the console shows a copyable curl snippet and a JSON payload. You can ingest that into Splunk/Datadog.

[04:00] Marco: (typing) Loading request logs — you can filter by route, user-id header, request-id, status, and time window. Here's a failed response — status 500 with stack-like message.
[04:12] Maya: The transcript from our agents sometimes jumble model names; will that appear?
[04:16] Marco: Transcription fields are auto-populated from the response; proper nouns can be off. We store raw model name and variant in metadata to avoid that.

[05:00] Marco: Going into Error Analysis tab — we group by root cause signature, e.g., OOM vs timeout vs decode error. You can click into aggregated examples and see sample prompts that triggered it.
[05:15] Jared: That sample prompt view will be helpful for QA. Can we attach prompt sets for regression monitoring?
[05:20] Marco: Yes, Redwood Optimize ties eval sets to routes so you can surface regressions when a new model or quantization is rolled out.

[06:00] Maya: Our infra team is worried about KV cache correctness — we sometimes see cold-start latencies.
[06:06] Marco: There is a cache hit/miss metric in the trace. For prefix cache, we show per-key hit ratio, median time saved, and suggestions for warmers.
[06:18] Aisha: One trick is to pre-warm hot prefixes during low traffic or use a small dedicated pool.

[07:00] Marco: (shows config) Here's the request logs JSON for one failing request — you can see timing breakdowns: queue wait, batching delay, model token time, and network.
[07:12] Samir: That batching delay field — how often does batching introduce extra latency for our 200ms SLO?
[07:18] Marco: Batching is workload-dependent. With reshaping and continuous batching, small requests might wait up to the batch window. You can reduce batch window or set SLO-aware routing so latency-sensitive requests go to low-latency pool.

[08:10] Marco: Quick demo — filter to route "payments-confirm" and set status=error. See aggregated stacks and top 5 offending prompts.
[08:22] Maya: Nice — can we anonymize PII in saved prompts? Our prompts include card last4 and transaction IDs.
[08:28] Marco: Yes, we support redaction and prompt anonymization rules; you can mask patterns or disable storing prompt text and only keep hashed fingerprints.

[09:00] Jared: On the Dedicated vs Hosted question — what's the tradeoff for us as a fintech?
[09:06] Aisha: Hosted is faster to start and cheaper at low volume. Dedicated gives you isolated GPUs, predictable latency, and data-at-rest isolation. With Dedicated you can also run inside your VPC for network controls.
[09:18] Samir: Do you offer an on-prem option or is it VPC only?
[09:21] Marco: We have a Private deployment option that can be installed in a customer-controlled environment for regulated workloads — that's typically an enterprise engagement.

[10:00] Marco: (shows audit logs) For security, Console has immutable audit logs, SSO with SAML/SCIM, role-based access, and KMS integration for model keys.
[10:12] Samir: Do audit logs include request bodies?
[10:15] Marco: They include metadata by default. You can configure retention and whether full payloads are stored; for high-sensitivity customers we recommend masking prompt text and storing hashes only.

[11:00] Maya: How does Redwood surface performance regressions over time?
[11:05] Marco: We have quality monitoring tied to eval sets and can chart metric drift (perplexity, hallucination rates) and alert on regressions with links to traces and sample prompts.

[12:10] Marco: Back to request logs — there is a quick query bar. You can paste multiple request-ids separated by comma and see side-by-side traces for comparison.
[12:22] Jared: That's helpful for debugging deploy rollouts. Can we correlate with model variant?
[12:26] Marco: Yep every trace includes model name, quantization bits, and kernel used.

[13:00] Marco: Now I'll demo a debugging flow: filter for 5xx, pick a representative trace, click into KV cache diagnostics — here we see a 40% miss rate on a hot prefix at 03:17 UTC.
[13:15] Maya: Could that be because our requests include a user-id that changes?
[13:18] Marco: Possibly — we suggest normalizing prefixes or tagging user-id in metadata rather than prompt text so cache keys are stable.

[14:00] Marco: Next I open the tracing waterfall for the request — see a long batching wait then a model spike. Looking at host metadata shows one host was on a different kernel, which increased token times.
[14:12] Aisha: That could be due to mixed-instance scaling; you can pin a pool to homogeneous hardware to avoid kernel variance.

[15:00] Samir: For encryption, we need to know where keys live. KMS/HSM integration details?
[15:05] Marco: We integrate with customer KMS for private deployments and with managed KMS for hosted. For Dedicated in a VPC we support customer-managed keys.

[16:00] Marco: (typing) Sending the sample trace JSON to the chat... you should see a link to download.
[16:06] Jared: Got it.

[18:00] Aisha: Let's talk about pilot design — we recommend a 2-hour window at peak traffic capture with full tracing on the payments-confirm route. Marco will share the benchmark template.
[18:12] Marco: The template includes request set, expected token distributions, and SLO targets. We'll also recommend batch window and caching config.

[20:00] Maya: Cost question — if we enable full capture, what's the storage/ingest cost?
[20:06] Aisha: Full capture costs scale with tokens captured and trace retention. We can run the pilot with a 7-day retention window and we will estimate costs in the perf spreadsheet.

[22:000] Marco: (shows Error Analysis) Here's how we triage frequent errors — you can create a workflow to automatically create JIRA tickets from a given error signature.
[22:12] Maya: That automation will save time for our engs.

[24:00] Jared: A quick one — does the console support exporting request logs to our S3?
[24:04] Marco: Yes, we have export connectors for S3, BigQuery, and Snowflake. You can set daily exports or stream via our events API.

[26:00] Samir: About compliance — we need SOC2 Type II report and network architecture diagram.
[26:06] Aisha: We'll send SOC2 and the network diagram as part of the security pack. I'll attach them to the CRM and email.

[28:00] Marco: Walkthrough of a debug session where we found a model variant causing hallucinations — you can pin routes to earlier model versions while investigating.
[28:12] Maya: Is rollback instantaneous?
[28:15] Marco: There's a near-instant rollback for routing; model loads depend on whether the variant is already warmed. For instant low-latency we recommend keeping a warm pool for the main variant.

[30:00] Jared: For the pilot, what telemetry should we collect on our side?
[30:06] Marco: Request-id mapping in your app logs, and a sample prompt set with normalized prefixes. Also CPU/GPU utilization from your side so we can correlate with kernel slowness.

[32:00] Marco: (shows timeline annotations) You can create notes on traces, tag them, and share a link to the team.
[32:10] Aisha: That helps when multiple teams are diagnosing the same issue.

[34:00] Maya: Any gotchas around model quantization we should know?
[34:05] Marco: Quantization can reduce memory and cost but sometimes impacts output quality. We recommend running A/B tests with Redwood Optimize and setting quality monitors to detect regressions.

[36:00] Jared: Overall this looks good. Next steps recap?
[36:05] Aisha: We'll send SOC2 + network diagram (Aisha), Marco will share benchmark template and perf spreadsheet, and we'll set up the 2-hour pilot once Jared confirms time window.
[36:20] Jared: I'll confirm by EOD tomorrow.

[38:00] Samir: One last item — retention window for request logs, we need 90 days for audit. Is that supported?
[38:08] Marco: Yes for enterprise customers you can configure retention up to 365 days; cost and storage considerations apply.

[40:00] Aisha: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and a proposed pilot schedule. Anything else?
[40:10] Maya: No, that's it. Thanks both.
[40:14] Jared: Thanks.
[41:30] (call ends)
